proposal.summary: In patrickfuller camp (up to commit bbd53a2) password.txt in the web root is served by StaticFileHandler despite a Tornado rule intended to return 403, and the password hash is reused as the application's cookie secret allowing an attacker to forge authentication cookies.
proposal.affected_product: patrickfuller camp up to and including commit bbd53a256ed70e79bd8758080936afbf6d738767
proposal.cwe_quote: Access to the password.txt file is not properly restricted as it is in the root directory served by StaticFileHandler and the Tornado rule to throw a 403 error when password.txt is accessed can be bypassed.

AV.quote: Access to the password.txt file is not properly restricted as it is in the root directory served by StaticFileHandler

PR.quote: Access to the password.txt file is not properly restricted as it is in the root directory served by StaticFileHandler and the Tornado rule to throw a 403 error when password.txt is accessed can be bypassed.

C.quote: the password hash is also used as the cookie secret, so an attacker can generate his own authentication cookie.

I.quote: the password hash is also used as the cookie secret, so an attacker can generate his own authentication cookie.

A.quote: the password hash is also used as the cookie secret, so an attacker can generate his own authentication cookie.

proposal.recommended_next_step: Verify the report by attempting to directly GET /password.txt from a deployed instance and confirm cookie forgery by generating a cookie using the disclosed hash; then remove password.txt from web root, enforce proper StaticFileHandler restrictions, and stop using password hashes as cookie secrets (generate a separate strong random secret and rotate session cookies).
